title: Jimmy Crawford, who urged him to come to New York
summary: Jones praises Jimmy Crawford's sweetening of the Lunceford sound and says Crawford begged him to come to New York.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Hey, you know who we didn't mention - Old Gal - Jimmy Crawford.

You mean the one I said, send-for to him? It's like preparing a meal. You can fix the cake but if you leave the sweetening out of it you ain't got no cake. He's the most beautiful man, you know. Naturally Mr. Lunceford had the long baton. The band's style involved itself loosely musically around Willie Smith but as a result the two-beat thing that Crawford did - you and I both knew a drummer by the name of Brown used to play at the Beale Street Theatre in Memphis. Crawford had the thing. Incidentally, without Jimmy Crawford do you know I never would have left Kansas City with Basie? He begged me, and here he is with Jimmy Lunceford. He says, you're coming to New York. I said, I'm not coming to New York. You know, I hadn't met Leroy Maxey..

You remember Maxey ? He was with Cab Calloway when I joined in '36. You remember Maxey, a great drummer. I'm glad you mentioned his name. I'll tell you another guy we didn't mention yet. Of course we haven't gotten to this one fellow I'd like to say right now.
